candidate_boot_identity.note: Every candidate 08 device capture in this stream carries this anchor. No capture from candidate 05, 06 or 07 is used anywhere in it.

reason: The operator was asked twice for the stimulus batch and was not able to speak either time. No wake-word utterance and no button press happened on candidate 08, so no detection run and no record/playback cycle were performed.
explicitly_not_a_failure: A window with no stimulus says nothing about a failure rate. Nothing here is recorded as 0/4 or as a negative result, and no gain, threshold, PGA or channel was touched.

not_borrowed_from_other_candidates.why: Candidate 08 changes both the microsecond-to-int16 conversion and the playback-time input consumer, so earlier candidate results cannot stand in for it in either direction.

operator_dependent_rows.input_continuity_during_playback: NOT_VERIFIED - tx_overlap_n was 0 in every window because the transmit path was never active
operator_dependent_rows.tx_overlap_sample_sufficiency: NOT_VERIFIED - no transmit activity to overlap with
operator_dependent_rows.reference_channel: NOT_VERIFIED - no playback cycle; candidate 05's claim about this channel was withdrawn as SUPERSEDED and candidate 08 has no measurement of its own
operator_dependent_rows.normal_volume_no_visible_clipping: OBSERVED, see normalisation_verification - no clipping occurred up to 78.92% of ADC full scale, but no controlled normal-volume speech stimulus was applied

normalisation_verification.why_this_is_independent_of_the_operator: raw_peak is the pre-shift ADC value and peak is the post-shift int16 value, both printed by the same window line, so the conversion can be checked arithmetically from any capture that contains input at all.
normalisation_verification.method: For every ch0 window, compare (raw_peak >> 16) with the reported peak.
normalisation_verification.result: peak equals raw_peak >> 16 in all 202 windows that carry input, out of 202 channel-0 windows; there is no additional scaling, rounding or dithering beyond the shift itself. No shifted value exceeds the int16 ceiling.

peak_observation.linearity: The two percentages agree to 0.01 percentage points, i.e. the int32-to-int16 conversion is full-width and lossless.

what_the_old_shift_would_have_done.consequence: Compulsory clipping for a large fraction of samples in that second.

named_limits: This verifies the conversion arithmetic under a real input event; it does not verify wake detection or playback, and it is not a substitute for a controlled normal-volume stimulus.
The input event at that timestamp is not attributed to speech: the operator was not speaking. What made the sound is unknown and irrelevant to the arithmetic.

candidate_05_worst_window.note: candidate 05 also reached ~2^31 but recorded 1098 clipped samples in a second

candidate_08_same_scale.note: at 78.92% of full scale candidate 08 records zero clipped samples

idle_only_observations.note: Per-capture totals across four captures from three separate boot sessions. These are not a continuous observation and no cross-capture sum is presented as a session total.

how_to_close: Operator present: in one capture, 4 wake-word utterances at 20-30cm normal volume >=3s apart; then at least two record-3s/playback cycles with a report of what was heard.
Then check wake detections plus re-arm, LOCAL_REFERENCE_PROBE_END drained, INPUT continuity during playback via tx_overlap_n, and HEALTH wake=1 after the probe ends.
result: NOT_VERIFIED on the operator-dependent audio rows; the int32-to-int16 normalisation is independently verified as lossless by arithmetic
